newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CFE up eight percent on upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CFE up eight percent on upgrades.

text.p: Shares in Belgian construction and dredging firm CFE extended Thursday's nine percent rise by another eight percent in early Brussels bourse trade on Friday, lifted by news of a number of broker upgrades.
By 0845 GMT CFE shares were up 7.81 percent at 12,075 francs, a record high.

Generale Bank said in an investor note late on Thursday it believed CFE's shares were worth more than 14,250 francs because of good earnings prospects at its DEME dredging unit and the possibility CFE could be sold by its controlling shareholders.
Brokerage Corluy & Co said earlier this week it also rated the shares a 'buy' because of the prospects at DEME.
Just like CFE, Belgian holding company Ackermans & Van Haaren holds 39 percent of DEME. But Ackerman's share, which has risen sharply so far this year, was 10 francs lower at 8,150 francs.
